- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% relative to prior peak.
- After a sharp price spike (≥ 5% from prior high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; cap forecast at +3% above peak or align with 10-day moving average.
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.2) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early 30-day horizon (first 5–7 days); apply +1–2% bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days and apply smoother transition (e.g., linear decay over 3 days).
- Mean reversion is evident in 10–15 day horizon: if forecast is > 2σ above mean, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence; if below, add 0.5–1.5% per day.
